mutations.before: const shape = migrations.map((m) => ({ id: m.id, checksum: checksum(m.sql) }));
mutations.after: const shape = migrations.map((m) => ({ id: m.id, checksum: m.id }));
mutations.because: The template name is the identity of the migration set, and the set includes each migration's SQL checksum, not only its id: migrate() refuses a migration edited after it ran and insists it ship as a new one, so an edited migration is a different set. Hash the ids alone and every run after an edit reuses the template built from the pre-edit SQL, so every test that clones it gets a schema that no longer matches what migrate() would apply — and the failure surfaces as a migration refusing an applied migration, in whichever test happens to hit it first, hours from the edit. This mutation is server-FREE on purpose: the test it must be caught by feeds templateName() synthetic migrations with the same ids and different SQL and expects a different name, so verify-manifests catches it in the local gate, where the Mac has no TEST_PG_URL and a server-only mutation would read as survived.
command: changes when a migration's SQL changes
